tool_input.prompt:
Review-fix task on PR #536 (bead ethos-5y4r). Repo <repo>, branch design/opencode-plugin-adapter, already checked out — do not create or switch branches. Commit on this branch; do not push, do not touch PRs or threads, do not merge — the leader does that. Write set: docs/design-opencode-plugin.md and DESIGN.md (DES-078) only. Commit by explicit path: `git commit -m <msg> -- docs/design-opencode-plugin.md DESIGN.md`; never stage or restore any other file. `make check` must pass before each commit. If source or the spec shows a change impossible, stop and report.

Two changes, both leader decisions:

1. C16 (authority: docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex, ledger C16 and its "Consequences for the design document" item, now model-checked and accepted). In §5 point 2 (claim-forked write phase) item 5 / the "do not retry" exit after the step-6 re-read of the mission (made under the step-5 locks): when the mission is found not open on the resume path, the call first closes the open dkFork skeleton the pending record names (owned by the child) with verdict aborted, as compare-and-set on verdict open under the delegation lock; a close that fails ends the call with the record kept as the retry token; the record is removed only after the close succeeds; then it exits "do not retry". Delete or correct any sentence saying the sweep closes what remains after a closed-mission exit — true of the locked sweep, false of the unlocked fallback of Store.Close (internal/mission/store.go ~1107-1114), whose snapshot may precede and whose write may follow the exit. Add the spec's required test. Update every count: "fifteen counterexamples (C1 to C15) and fifteen fix switches", "all fifteen switches" (around design-opencode-plugin.md:199-203 and the exit-status table row near ~2233, plus any in DESIGN.md) to sixteen / C1 to C16, naming fixResumeClosed. Note the coverage limits the spec now states: the unlocked sweep is exhaustively checked on the claim-u/claim+u slices, not combined with the chain initialisation, and the full-machine rows stay bounded below depth 12.

2. Copilot finding (PR #536 comment 4355630240): "Reserve the ID when the pending record is persisted, rather than waiting for the skeleton. If the record write succeeds but the skeleton write fails, `releaseID(false)` can return that ID to the counter (internal/mission/id.go:205-222) while the record still names it. Another Tier B dispatch under the same mission can then acquire it; this child's retry satisfies the documented resume checks and binds itself to that unrelated delegation. Keep the allocation consumed once any durable record references it, and cover a failed skeleton write followed by ID allocation and retry." Read id.go to confirm the mechanism. Amend the design: once the claim-forked-pending record naming a delegation ID is durably written, that ID is consumed (the allocation is committed, never released by releaseID(false)), on every later failure path. Add the required test: record write succeeds, skeleton write fails, a second dispatch allocates an ID (must differ), then the child's retry resumes its own ID and does not bind to the other delegation. Mirror both changes in DES-078 in DESIGN.md.

Grep both files afterward for "fifteen", "C15", and any statement that the ID is released on skeleton failure; fix each. Report the commit hash(es) and a line-cited summary.
